chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Isa ibn Suleiman, from Bakkar ibn Kardam, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man meets a woman and says to her, 'Marry yourself to me for a month,' and he does not specify the particular month. Then he goes away and meets her after years. He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'For him is his month if he had specified it, and if he did not specify it, there is no way for him upon her.'

key_terms.زَوِّجِينِي: Marry yourself to me (imperative form used in marriage contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a temporary marriage contract where the duration is vague or unspecified?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the essential condition of specificity in the duration of temporary marriage (mut'ah), distinguishing between a vague reference to 'a month' and a precise designation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that ambiguity in the time frame invalidates the binding nature of the contract upon the woman, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that key elements of the contract must be clearly defined to ensure mutual consent and prevent dispute. This ruling underscores the importance of precision in contractual terms within Shia fiqh, ensuring that the rights of both parties are protected against uncertainty (gharar).
